title: Prayer is a chief part of divine worship, so angels and saints are not to be invoked
source_text: LXXXIX. Caeterum nec Angelos, nec Beatos justorum Spiritus precandos & invocandos esse ex eo constat, quod Scriptura sacra Orationem & invocationem pro insigni cultus divini parte habet, & eximio atque praecipuo nostrae Religionis erga Deum officio. Unde est quod templum Dei in Scriptura dicitur Domus Orationis; & fidelium preces atque orationes ut spirituale quoddam sacrificium proponuntur; & eum solum docemur invocare in quem fides nostra recumbit. Juxta illud Apostoli Quomodo invocabunt in quem non crediderunt? Es. 56. 7. Matth. 21. 13. Psal. 141. 2. Heb. 13. 15. Rom. 10. 14.
pass_a_gloss: But moreover that neither Angels, nor the Blessed Spirits of the just, are to be prayed to and invoked is established from this, that sacred Scripture holds Prayer and invocation for a notable part of divine worship, and for a special and principal duty of our Religion toward God. Whence it is that the temple of God is called in Scripture the House of Prayer; and the prayers and petitions of the faithful are set forth as a certain spiritual sacrifice; and we are taught to invoke him alone on whom our faith rests. According to that of the Apostle How shall they invoke him in whom they have not believed? Isaiah 56:7. Matthew 21:13. Psalm 141:2. Hebrews 13:15. Romans 10:14.
pass_b_english: That neither angels nor the blessed spirits of the just are to be prayed to or invoked is settled by this: Scripture counts prayer and invocation a principal part of divine worship and a chief and special duty of our religion toward God.

That is why Scripture calls God's temple "the house of prayer" (Isaiah 56:7; Matthew 21:13), and sets the prayers and supplications of the faithful before us as a kind of spiritual sacrifice (Psalm 141:2; Hebrews 13:15). And we are taught to call only on him in whom our faith rests, as the Apostle says: "How shall they call on him in whom they have not believed?" (Romans 10:14).

lemmas.gloss: as a notable part of divine worship

choices.why: Recumbit is the language of reliance; 'rests' keeps it without adding a doctrine.
